reviewers.role: Prüferin (lizenzierte Goethe-A2-Prüferin): exam fidelity, rubric application, task clarity
Kursleiterin DaF/DaZ, Niveau A2.2: naturalness, level, didactics, scene plausibility

method: Every German string was read: start, LS1-LS3 inputs, items, pools, reserves, micro-outputs and Aussprache; LS4 texts and blocks; LS5/LS6 Aufgaben; check, proofs, redemittel, story and fokus. Every item was solved blind from promptDe plus options, tiles or audio line, and then compared with answer and accepted[]. Both exam blocks, the writing task and the speaking task were checked against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/ga2.json (h1, l4, s1, sp3). The grammar ceiling was checked against grammar-spine.json, the lexicon allocation against curriculum/a2-2.md E4 and a2.2/lexicon.json, the can-dos against registries/cando/a2.json, and the cast against casts/a2.json and casts/series.json. Validator: node scripts/course-v2/validate.mjs content/course-v2/a2.2/units/u04.json returned FAIL (3 LEX-03 blocker, 30 LEX-02 ratchet, 9 GRM-04 advisory). node scripts/course-v2/check.mjs returned 0 errors.
verdict: Not exitable in round 1. Validator: 1 blocker, a false positive that still fails CI. Manual review: 7 MAJOR, 12 MINOR. No answer key is wrong and no exam block has the wrong item or option counts. h1 (5 texts, 3 options, 2 plays, 53-60 words) and l4 (5 items, 6 ads, X, 34-41 words) are template-exact, and s1 (SMS, 3 Leitpunkte, 20-30 words, ga2-s1) is correct. The majors are: a false rule repeated in three explanations ("es wird – ohne d"); a correct answer class that is not accepted (gegenüber + dative without von, four items); an unlevelled lexicon allocation (entlang); a story geography that makes the unit's model emergency call report the wrong place; and a Sprechen Teil 3 stimulus that is not a Tageskalender and makes finding a time trivial.

findings.quote: LEX-03 x unknown lemma form(s) in a answer: f | c | X
findings.problem: validate.mjs FAILs the unit on LEX-03 (3 blocker). The keys are correct: a zuordnen item's answer is a choice letter (f, c) or the noMatchKey (X), and LEX-03 wrongly checks them as German lemmas. The keys a and b pass only by accident. The unit content needs no change, but as long as the rule misfires the file cannot pass CI.
findings.fix: Rule-side (scripts/course-v2 LEX-03): skip answers of items whose type is zuordnen/abc/multiple_choice when the answer is a key of block.choices or equals block.noMatchKey. Do not edit the unit to work around it.
findings.proposedRule: LEX-03 ignores choice-key answers (block.choices[].key ∪ block.noMatchKey), with a fixture of a ga2.l4 block whose keys are f and X.

findings.quote: es wird – ohne d am Ende. / es wird dunkel – ohne d. / es wird – ohne d.
findings.problem: The explanation is false: wird ends in d. The ohne-d rule holds only for du wirst (not *wirdst*). The typical er/es error is *wirdt* or *wirt*, so the real contrast is "with d, no t". A learner who writes wird correctly is told the opposite of what they see. The source rule card rc.werden-vollverb (a2.2/rule-cards.json, other owner) makes the same claim ("du wirst und er wird – ohne d am Ende"), so this is a class.
findings.fix: ls2-p01/ls2-r01/c03: "es wird – mit d am Ende, aber ohne t." (en: "es wird – ends in d, no t."). Keep "du wirst – ohne d" for ls2-p02/ls2-p10/ls2-s03. Report the rule-card sentence to its owner: "Achtung: du wirst (ohne d), er/sie/es wird (ohne t)."
findings.proposedRule: Lint: an explanation or rule card that pairs a token ending in d (wird) with "ohne d" fails. Fixture: "es wird – ohne d".

findings.quote: Die Tankstelle ist gegenüber ___ Rathaus. / Gegenüber ___ Kiosk gibt es eine Apotheke. / Die Haltestelle ist gegenüber ___ Bahnhof.
findings.problem: accepted[] = [vom, von dem]. "gegenüber dem Rathaus / dem Kiosk / dem Bahnhof" is standard German (gegenüber + Dativ, Duden) and is the more formal written form. The unit's own rule card writes "gegenüber (von) mit Dativ". A learner who follows the card and types dem is marked wrong in a check item. Only the English promptEn ("gegenüber von + …") excludes it, and the German prompt does not.
findings.fix: Add "dem" to accepted[] with acceptedWhy {"dem": "gegenüber + Dativ ohne von ist auch richtig"} and reviewerConfirmed as the schema requires. Extend the explanation: "gegenüber vom Bahnhof oder gegenüber dem Bahnhof".
findings.proposedRule: ITM-10 extension: a fill_blank whose gap directly follows "gegenüber" and whose key is a von+article contraction (vom) must also accept the bare dative article (dem).

findings.quote: Tomasz ruft die 112 an. Bald kommt der ___.
findings.problem: The German prompt does not determine the key. "Bald kommt der Notarzt" is equally correct and is the unit's own lemma (lx.notarzt), and the dispatcher says it in the same input: "ein Notarzt kommt auch". "Rettungswagen" is also correct. Only the English promptEn ("the vehicle …") narrows the answer to Krankenwagen, but items must be solvable from the German.
findings.fix: Make the German prompt decide: "Tomasz ruft die 112 an. Bald kommt der ___ und bringt Lina ins Krankenhaus." Also accept "Rettungswagen" with acceptedWhy. Alternatively accept "Notarzt".

findings.quote: Korrigieren Sie: „Du gehst bis zu die Brücke.“ → accepted: ["Du gehst bis zur Brücke."]
findings.problem: The minimal correction "Du gehst bis zu der Brücke." is grammatical, and the unit accepts "zu der" in ls1-p02, q01 and the rule card. The error-correction item rejects exactly the form a learner produces by fixing only the article.
findings.fix: Add "Du gehst bis zu der Brücke." to accepted[] with acceptedWhy "grammatisch richtig, man sagt aber fast immer zur".
findings.proposedRule: ITM-10: when a unit accepts an uncontracted form (zu der, von dem) in a fill_blank, every error_correction whose answer contains the contraction (zur, vom) must accept the uncontracted sentence too.

findings.path: steps[2].input.lines[1] (ls3-l02), lines[10] (ls3-l11); steps[2].inputItems[4] (ls3-i05); steps[2].reserve[3] (ls3-r04); check.lines[2] + redemittel[2]
findings.quote: „Wir stehen an der Brücke für Fußgänger, gegenüber vom Kiosk.“ … „Mein Freund geht zur Tankstelle an der Straße und wartet dort.“
findings.problem: The story geography contradicts itself, and the emergency call models reporting the wrong place. LS1: Tankstelle opposite the Rathaus → Kiosk → turn left → through the park → bridge at the far end, so the bridge cannot be opposite the kiosk. LS2: the group has already left the bridge and is hiking along the river beyond the hill ("hinter dem Hügel wird der Weg jetzt steil", Wiese am Ufer) when Lina slips. So Tomasz reports the meeting point, not the accident site, and sends someone back to a petrol station on the far side of the park. Giving a precise location is the first thing the unit teaches for 112, and here the model fails it.
findings.fix: Make the location match LS2. ls3-l02: "Wir sind am Fluss, am Ufer hinter dem Hügel. Zur Brücke für Fußgänger sind es zehn Minuten." ls3-l11: "Mein Freund geht zurück zur Brücke und wartet dort." Then change ls3-i05 (key Brücke), ls3-r04 ("Emre wartet ___ Brücke", key "an der") and ls3-s01 accordingly. Also either move the kiosk next to the bridge in LS1 ("Am Ende vom Park ist ein Kiosk, die Brücke ist gegenüber") or reword rm03/check line l03 so that they do not claim bridge-opposite-kiosk.

findings.quote: Ihr Kalender: Freitag 17 Uhr Deutschkurs · Samstag 9–14 Uhr arbeiten · Samstag 19 Uhr Geburtstag · Sonntag: frei | Amal: … Sonntag: frei, ab 18 Uhr zu Hause
findings.problem: Goethe A2 Sprechen Teil 3 gives each candidate a different Tageskalender for one day, with hourly entries. The pair must negotiate the single free window, and that negotiation is the scored behaviour (the template source reads "zwei verschiedene Tageskalender, einen Termin finden"). Here the stimulus is a sparse three-day list in which both people are free all Sunday, so the time is settled in one turn and the Teil's core move is never practised. This is a .2 course, so lane fidelity is required. EXM-04 passes because it checks only the mode, the stimulus kind and the rubric.
findings.fix: Replace both stimuli with one-day calendars for the same day (for example Sonntag, 8–20 Uhr), 5–6 entries each, leaving exactly one shared 2–3-hour window (for example 11–14 Uhr). Keep the follow-up (Wohin? Wie? Was mitnehmen? Wer macht was?). Adjust modelTurns to show one refusal and one counter-proposal on the time. Remove "ab 18 Uhr zu Hause", which is unclear.
findings.proposedRule: EXM-04 for ga2.sp3: stimulus and partnerData are day calendars for the same single day with ≥ 5 timed entries each and exactly one overlapping free window of ≥ 90 minutes.

findings.quote: lx.entlang (role productive, unit a2.2-u04) · „Wir fahren mit dem Fahrrad immer am Ufer …“
findings.problem: The binding level plan (curriculum/a2-2.md E4) says: "entlang and um … herum are not taught here: memo 06 F3 places them in B1.2". The unit still allocates entlang as a productive lemma. It occurs 0 times in the unit's inputs (LEX-02), so a productive word is counted, tested by generators and reviewed without ever being taught. Avoiding the word also left ad t6 unidiomatic: "immer am Ufer" needs "entlang".
findings.fix: Remove lx.entlang from lexiconBlocks[0] and replace it with a plan keyword (die Richtung or der Treffpunkt), which the owner of a2.2/lexicon.json and specs.json must mirror. Rephrase t6: "Wir fahren mit dem Fahrrad auf dem Weg am Fluss und machen am Mittag ein Picknick …".
findings.proposedRule: LEX-05/plan check: a lemma the level plan marks as 'not taught here' must not be allocated in that unit; productive lemmas with 0 input occurrences fail (hard, not ratchet).

findings.quote: det.zustandspassiv „sind … verletzt“, „ist … gebrochen“, „ist … verletzt“; det.konjunktiv1 „Park gehe“, „Sonntag habe“; det.adjektiv-endung-nullartikel „eine“, „unser“, „kleinen“
findings.problem: Reviewed one by one. Eight are false positives. "verletzt/gebrochen sein" is an adjectival participle and a plan keyword (verletzt). "gehe/habe" are 1st-person indicative. "eine Jacke" and "unser Boot" have no adjective. The only real look-ahead is "mit kleinen Kindern" in exam ad t9: adjective without article, dative plural, licensed from a2.2-u05, one unit later. It is receptive, so minor.
findings.fix: t9: "Unser Kurs für Mütter und Väter mit Babys und Kleinkindern" (no adjective). Rule-side: exempt ich-forms from det.konjunktiv1, and add a detector hint for verletzt/gebrochen/kaputt + sein.
findings.proposedRule: det.konjunktiv1 requires a 3rd-person subject; det.adjektiv-endung-nullartikel requires an ADJ token.

findings.quote: 6 Anzeigen, 5 Items, kein Beispiel
findings.problem: In Goethe A2 Lesen Teil 4 one ad is used up by the Beispiel (0), so candidates face 5 items, 5 remaining ads and one X, which leaves one unused ad. Here there is no example, so two ads (d, e) are unused. That adds one distractor and changes the elimination logic. Counts match the template, and the template itself notes "die Anzeige aus dem Beispiel ist verbraucht".
findings.fix: Add a Beispiel person (0) that is answered and consumes ad d or e. The schema and template owner needs to model block.example, so this is a class fix.
findings.proposedRule: EXM-01 for ga2.l4: block.example present and its key not reused by items.

findings.quote: „Lina geht es wieder gut.“ … „Lina kann aber noch nicht gut laufen.“
findings.problem: The task says Lina is fine again, while the partner persona and the model turn build the disagreement on her still being unable to walk.
findings.fix: situationDe: "Lina geht es schon besser, aber sie kann noch nicht weit laufen."

findings.quote: „Ihre Freundin Amal … kennt den Weg von der Haltestelle nicht.“
findings.problem: Amal walked exactly this route in the start episode (Haltestelle vor dem Rathaus → Brücke), so the premise contradicts the story. Also, Leitpunkt 1 gives no landmarks, so the learner must invent a route, and the new prepositions (vorbei, bis zu, gegenüber) are not elicited by any stimulus.
findings.fix: Address someone new to the route (for example "Ihre Kollegin Anna" or a neighbour) and add a one-line landmark list to situationDe: "Haltestelle Rathaus – Tankstelle – Kiosk – Park – Brücke".

findings.quote: „Mein Handy ist bei dem Unfall kaputtgegangen.“
findings.problem: Lina writes to the group at 18.30 and again in the evening, and says in that same message that her phone broke in the accident.
findings.fix: "Das Display von meinem Handy ist bei dem Unfall kaputtgegangen, ich kann kaum etwas lesen." Alternatively have her write from the Webers' phone.

findings.quote: Priya/Amal: „Wir sind an der Haltestelle vor dem Rathaus.“ … Lina: „Jetzt stehe ich an der Haltestelle vor dem Rathaus.“
findings.problem: Priya and Amal have waited at that stop for ten minutes, yet Lina arrives at the same stop and Emre phones her with directions instead of the three walking together. The scene is constructed rather than lived, which is an H issue.
findings.fix: Put Lina at a different stop (for example "an der Haltestelle am Bahnhof") or have Priya say "Lina kommt gleich mit der nächsten Bahn, wir warten auf sie". Emre can then explain the route to Lina in LS1 from a different starting point.

findings.quote: „Mein Nachbar ist heute nicht so gut.“
findings.problem: This distractor is unidiomatic German on a surface the learner reads ("jemand ist nicht gut" ≠ "es geht ihm nicht gut"). Distractors should be correct German that is wrong for the situation.
findings.fix: "Meinem Nachbarn geht es heute nicht so gut."

findings.quote: pf: „Pfad|fad“, „Pflug|Flug“, „Pfeil|feil“ · readAloud „Du gehst über die Straße …“ · „st … im Wort wie st (Fenster)“
findings.problem: LS1 uses rare or archaic contrast words (fad, feil, Pflug) at A2, and its read-aloud line contains no pf. The LS3 rule "im Wort wie st" is false for prefixed and compound words the unit itself uses (auf|stehen in ls3-l10 and check l01). The focus names sp, but no sp item exists.
findings.fix: LS1 pairs: keep Pfund|Fund and replace the rare pairs with known pf-words heard against f/p (Pferd, Pflaster, Kopf, Apfel);readAloud: "Nehmen Sie ein Pflaster und einen Apfel mit." LS3 rule: "am Wort- oder Silbenanfang wie scht (Stein, aufstehen), sonst st (Fenster)" plus one sp item (sprechen).

findings.quote: speaker: cast.ensemble-a2-4
findings.problem: cast.ensemble-a2-4 shares Tomasz's voice (de-DE-RalfNeural), and casts/a2.json says "nicht in Szenen mit Tomasz – gleiche Stimme". Tomasz speaks in LS2/LS3 and is named in t2 of the same Prüfung, so the radio presenter will sound like Tomasz.
findings.fix: speaker "radio" (as t4), or another ensemble voice.

findings.quote: q01 fill_blank „bis ___ Ampel“; q02 multiple_choice
findings.problem: Both can-dos are interaction-spoken, but their proofs are a one-word gap and a recognition item. They are rehearsed only in the 30-40 s micro-outputs mo1/mo3. The spec's "später erzählen alle, wie es passiert ist" is not realised in any step (only Lina's two-line SMS).
findings.fix: Prove weg-erklaeren with mo1 and unfall-melden with mo3 (spoken, rubric course-micro-sp), or add a produced proof item: a typed 2-sentence 112 report with Wo? and Was ist passiert?.

findings.quote: „Die Regeln sind nicht in jeder Firma gleich.“
findings.problem: The core rules for a Wegeunfall are statutory and the same in every firm: it is covered by the gesetzliche Unfallversicherung, you tell the doctor it was on the way to work (Durchgangsarzt), and you report it to the employer. Only internal forms differ. The sentence suggests otherwise, and the fokus carries no fact record.
findings.fix: "Sagen Sie auch beim Arzt: Es war ein Unfall auf dem Weg zur Arbeit. Die Formulare sind in jeder Firma anders." Add a facts[] record (source DGUV, checkedOn, verification) and reference it in factRefs.

findings.quote: „Die Tankstelle ist gegenüber. Wo ist sie?“ · „Die Tour … fährt unter vielen Brücken durch.“ · „einen Kurs in Erster Hilfe“ · „besonders an Amal, Tomasz und Emre“ · errorTag spelling-meaning
findings.problem: Several small wording issues. In s02, sie can refer to Lina or the Tankstelle, and the explanation "direkt vor Lina" is odd. In t7, a tour does not "fahren"; the boat does. "Erste-Hilfe-Kurs" is the usual collocation. Lina's thanks single out everyone except Priya. c08 is a conjugation error tagged spelling-meaning.
findings.fix: s02: "Wo ist die Tankstelle?" + explanation "auf der anderen Seite der Straße". t7: "Das Boot fährt eine Stunde unter vielen Brücken hindurch." LS2: "Ich habe einen Erste-Hilfe-Kurs gemacht." SMS: "Danke für eure Hilfe, ihr wart super!"

passed: ga2.h1: 5 items, 3 options, plays 2 (instruction says zweimal), texts 53-60 words (band 35-75), text types radio/Mailbox/Durchsage/Anrufbeantworter, modeDefault pruefung, all keys verified.

ga2.l4: 5 items, 6 ads a-f, noMatch X on item 5, ads 34-41 words (band 25-45), about 226 words in total; keys a, f, b, c, X verified blind, and each distractor ad is excluded by day, audience or duration.
ga2.s1: SMS, informell/du, 3 Leitpunkte, 20-30 words, rubric ga2-s1, examKey goethe_a2; modelText is 29 words and covers all three points.
ga2.sp3: mode plan-together, prep 0, rubric ga2-sp3, learner-leads (see F07 for the stimulus).
No task copies a Goethe Modellsatz; every text is original, in the official format, and set in the unit's story.
Register: every instruction uses Sie; dialogues between the friends use du; the dispatcher and Tomasz use Sie.

Grammar ceiling: werden-Vollverb and the local prepositions enter at their spine position; deshalb, denn, wenn, the indirect question (wie Sie helfen können), Konjunktiv II (würde gern) and the reflexive (sich verletzen) are all licensed earlier.
Legal: no pass promise, no claim of human feedback.
